# Synapse 2.0.2

A fix release on top of 2.0.1. Synapse AI plans the services you name and tells you every part of what it will and won't build, the browser behaves better from sign-in to recording, and the website chat widget shows formatted replies with links you can click.

## Fixed

### Synapse AI and the builder

- **Services you name are planned, not hunted for.** Ask for a workflow that uses GitHub, Stripe or any other service and Synapse AI plans it straight away: with the tools you already have connected, with the app from the Apps catalogue (connected after you say yes), or with tools it looks up after the plan. It no longer spends calls searching for a provider first.
- **A plan lists every part of what you asked.** The plan card says which parts it builds, which it runs once after building, and which it won't do and why. When you asked for a run, a **Run it** card comes up once the workflow is built. It runs only when you press it, since a run uses credits.
- **A failed build says what to do.** When a model call fails for a reason we can name, such as a model CLI that isn't signed in, isn't installed or hit its limit, a provider with no address set, or Ollama not reachable, the build says that, not "The model call failed." An address in that message shows only its host and port, never a login or key.
- **An unknown model id is said plainly.** A model written as `anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6` (a provider and a dot) is reported as unknown with the id it most likely means, and nothing is called.
- **A spec too big to read says so.** An API spec over the 2 MB a build reads gets a clear message, and the app from the Apps catalogue when there is one.
- **No more stuck plan card.** Letting two tools act without asking, one after the other, no longer leaves the second plan's **Build it** disabled.
- **Synapse AI knows about Browser agents.** When you ask for something on a website with no API, it says it has no browser of its own, but a Browser agent does, and offers to make one.

### Browser

- **Typing reaches a slow browser whole and in order,** and an input that doesn't reach the page is said, not lost.
- **Keep** in the sign-in browser comes alive once a page has opened, and says why it waits until then.
- **A new sign-in opens the page you typed** on the site you named, over https, not only its front page.
- **A site the browser will never open is refused before any browser starts,** with the reason.
- **A blocked page shows its own reason,** and the browser's guard says its own words (not found, not public, could not be checked).
- **A site added to a Browser agent starts with your only session** for it, when you have exactly one.
- **Recordings have names.** You're asked for one when you stop, filled in from the site and its last step, and a recording can be renamed on its page.
- **A recorded click on an unlabelled checkbox reads as the words beside it,** never "on".
- **A browser that's slow to open says why:** the first one can take half a minute or so.
- **A Browser agent answers in its own words,** and is asked again if it repeats the page it read instead of answering.
- The Browser agent's mode is now labelled **What it may do on a page**.

### Website chat widget

- **Replies are formatted.** An agent's reply shows bold text, lists, tables and links you can click. Links open in a new tab, and only `https`, `http` and `mailto` links are made. Raw HTML and images in a reply are never drawn.

### Everywhere else

- **Model pickers find what you type** by the start of any word in a model's name, id or provider, with the best match first.
- **Settings keep what you type.** The General, Models, Integrations and Personal details tabs no longer put fields back to their saved values while you're editing.
- **No code-index database, no noise.** With no code-index database set, startup no longer tries one and prints an error.

## Install

**macOS and Linux**

```bash
curl -LsSf https://synapseorch.com/install.sh | bash
```

**Windows (PowerShell)**

```powershell
irm https://synapseorch.com/install.ps1 | iex
```

<details>
<summary>npm, pip or Docker</summary>

```bash
npm install -g synapse-orch-ai && synapse
pip install synapse-orch-ai && synapse         # Python 3.11–3.14 and Node.js 20.9+
```

For Docker, see [Docker](https://docs.synapseorch.com/getting-started/docker): the image is `synapseorchai/synapse-ai:2.0.2`, also `:latest`.
</details>

## Upgrading

- **From 2.0.0 or 2.0.1:** run `synapse upgrade`. Your data stays where it is, and the database is backed up first.
- **From 1.x:** run `synapse upgrade` on your 1.x install. It moves you to 2.0 the same way 2.0.0 did; read the [2.0.0 notes](https://github.com/synapseorch-ai/synapse-ai/releases/tag/v2.0.0) for what changes.
